dukkhasutta:
[Dukkha+sutta] (na) CL=9 Dukkha Sutta: (a) Sutta in which the craving that is the cause of suffering, and Nibbāna that is the cessation of suffering are preached in detail. (b) the Sutta in which how to attain Arattaphala is shown, having liberated from defilements because of contemplating on the suffering of five aggregates and removing the attachment to five aggregates.
(c) 1.having no faith; 2.no shame; 3.no fear,  4.laziness, 5.ignorance. One who possesses these five factors,  has to encounter suffering and miserable even in the present life and has to reborn in the woeful states after death. On the contrary, if he is not so, he has to feel enjoyment in this life and has to reborn in blissful abodes after death.
(d) 1.Kāmavitakka, 2.Byāpādavitakka, 3.Vihiṃsāvitakka, 4.Kāmasaññā, 5.Byāpādasaññā, 6.Vihiṃsāsaññā. One who possesses these six factors has to encounter suffering and miserable even in the present life and has to reborn in the woeful states after death. 1.nekkhammavitakka, 2.abyāpādavitakka, 3.avihiṃsāvitakka, 4.nekkhammasaññā, 5.abyāpādasaññā, 6.avihiṃsāsaññā- - one who possesses these six factors has to feel enjoyment in this life and has to reborn in blissful abodes after death.  All these about are preached in detail in this Sutta.
(e) this Sutta Shown as before;
one who meditates on volitional formations as happiness is not able to reach to Anulomikakhantīñāṇa and who is not perfect with this Anulomikakhantīñāṇa cannot attain Sammattaniyāma. if it is so, he will not realize four Phalas.
Only those who meditate on all volitional formations as suffering will be able to fulfill these six Dhammas.
